# Wording branches of the v13 text (generated by wording_v13.py --branches)

Each slot is shown under the base case (every status at its first value) and then once for each other value of each status, where that changes the text. Value placeholders are left unfilled.

## ABSTRACT

- **base**: We test whether a Kalman tracker's covariance, as a planner's safety margin, beats a class-average margin at equal caution, with an oracle and an oracle rank-matched at the tracker's amplitude as controls, on fresh CARLA runs scored once under a locked plan, in closed loop and on held-out nuScenes logs. The oracle's room is @@C:LB.R|pp@@ @@C:LB.R.ci|ci2@@ percentage points, and the score detects information at the tracker's amplitude. The tracker's covariance is equivalent to a class-average margin within 5% of the room on fresh runs, at cut-in events and on real logs; it was not shown equivalent in closed loop, where it is safer at no extra cost. An interacting-multiple-model tracker's covariance recovers @@C:LB.IMM.r|sh3@@ of the room, @@C:LB.IMM.eff|sh3@@ of its ceiling. A 3 m/s² braking prediction recovers most of the room (@@C:LB.RR_CK3|sh3@@) behind leads that brake to a stop but costs progress behind constant-speed, mildly braking and stop-and-go leads; so does a per-phase margin schedule (@@C:LB.PS.rec|sh3@@ of the room). In closed loop, where the car brakes as it can, the braking prediction is safer at no extra cost. Magnitudes depend on 2 Hz updates, filter tuning and the recording policy; removing covariance margins is not justified. Open-loop scores should state commitment, population and recording policy and show detection at the output's amplitude.

## TITLE

- **base**: Do Tracker Covariances Improve Planning Decisions? An Equal-Caution Test on Fresh Simulation Runs, in Closed Loop and on Real Driving Logs
- **E = stopped_brake**: Do Tracker Covariances Improve Planning Decisions? An Equal-Caution Test on Fresh Simulation Runs and on Real Driving Logs
- **F = design_only**: Do Tracker Covariances Improve Planning Decisions? An Equal-Caution Test on Fresh Simulation Runs and in Closed Loop
- **H3 = inconclusive**: Do Fixed-Noise and Interacting-Multiple-Model Tracker Covariances Improve Planning Decisions? An Equal-Caution Test on Fresh Simulation Runs, in Closed Loop and on Real Driving Logs

## INTRO_DATA

- **base**: Here we test on data not used for any design choice: fresh CARLA runs in two scenario families, lead braking and cut-in, recorded and scored once under a plan fixed in advance; a closed-loop test in which the margin sources drive the car; and held-out nuScenes logs [110].
- **E = stopped_brake**: Here we test on data not used for any design choice: fresh CARLA runs in two scenario families, lead braking and cut-in, recorded and scored once under a plan fixed in advance; a closed-loop test, attempted and stopped when the car's braking did not meet the planner's model; and held-out nuScenes logs [110].
- **E = stopped_other**: Here we test on data not used for any design choice: fresh CARLA runs in two scenario families, lead braking and cut-in, recorded and scored once under a plan fixed in advance; a closed-loop test, attempted and stopped before its main runs; and held-out nuScenes logs [110].
- **F = design_only**: Here we test on data not used for any design choice: fresh CARLA runs in two scenario families, lead braking and cut-in, recorded and scored once under a plan fixed in advance; a closed-loop test in which the margin sources drive the car; and nuScenes logs [110], on their design split only.
- **F = no_room_design**: Here we test on data not used for any design choice: fresh CARLA runs in two scenario families, lead braking and cut-in, recorded and scored once under a plan fixed in advance; a closed-loop test in which the margin sources drive the car; and nuScenes logs [110], which showed no measurable room on their design split.
- **F = omitted**: Here we test on data not used for any design choice: fresh CARLA runs in two scenario families, lead braking and cut-in, recorded and scored once under a plan fixed in advance; and a closed-loop test in which the margin sources drive the car.

## RUNS_FRESH

- **base**: Fresh runs come from never-run cases of the same generator: @@C:LB.n_runs|int@@ lead-braking and @@C:CI.n_runs|int@@ cut-in runs, 35 per desired speed of 5, 10 and 15 m/s in each family, and @@D:D1.n_runs|int@@ runs behind leads that do not brake hard, recorded like the old evaluation runs with all lidar sweeps kept and scored once after the plan was locked (failed runs were replaced as the plan prescribes; Supplement S3).

## CL_BUILD

- **base**: In the closed-loop test the planner drives the ego in CARLA with each margin source as an arm, on @@E:E3.n_cases|int@@ fresh lead-braking cases and @@E:E3b.n_cases|int@@ cases behind non-braking leads. CARLA's speed controller does not brake as the planner assumes, so a feed-forward correction of the acceleration servo was added, gated by a brake test fixed in advance: stops from 5, 10 and 15 m/s within 10% of the planner's model. The test passed (largest error @@E:E1.maxerr|pct0@@). A calibration on tuning cases set two margin levels at which F0's contact share was near 0.20 and 0.05; every other arm was set to the scale whose open-loop caution matches F0's there. Outcomes per run are contact, impact speed, time lost against the desired speed, peak deceleration, jerk and the share of decisions in full braking; each arm is compared with F0 at the same level, paired by case, and the IMM with its own class average.
- **E = stopped_brake**: A closed-loop test, with the margin sources as arms of the planner driving the ego in CARLA, was attempted. CARLA's speed controller does not brake as the planner assumes, so a feed-forward correction of the acceleration servo was added, gated by a brake test fixed in advance: stops from 5, 10 and 15 m/s within 10% of the planner's model. The car stopped @@E:E1.v5.err|pct0@@, @@E:E1.v10.err|pct0@@ and @@E:E1.v15.err|pct0@@ from the model's distance at the three speeds, so by the plan the closed-loop study stopped there (Supplement S9).
- **E = stopped_other**: A closed-loop test, with the margin sources as arms of the planner driving the ego in CARLA, was attempted. CARLA's speed controller does not brake as the planner assumes, so a feed-forward correction of the acceleration servo was added, gated by a brake test fixed in advance: stops from 5, 10 and 15 m/s within 10% of the planner's model. The test passed, but the main runs did not finish by the plan's deadline (Supplement S9).

## RL_BUILD

- **base**: The open-loop test is replicated on nuScenes [110]. CenterPoint detections (of unconfirmed provenance) are tracked by CANMOT with its released nuScenes configuration and by the IMM tracker, and the planner is applied through an adapter: the route is the ego's logged path, and truth boxes are interpolated between annotated keyframes. Class averages and the commitment horizon were set on the training scenes, on which the detector was trained. The @@F:F.n_heldout|int@@ held-out validation scenes were scored once, with a @@F:F.horizon|str@@ s commitment, the longer of 3 and 2 s at which the training scenes showed room.
- **F = design_only**: The open-loop test is replicated on nuScenes [110]. CenterPoint detections (of unconfirmed provenance) are tracked by CANMOT with its released nuScenes configuration and by the IMM tracker, and the planner is applied through an adapter: the route is the ego's logged path, and truth boxes are interpolated between annotated keyframes. Class averages and the commitment horizon were set on the training scenes, on which the detector was trained. The held-out analysis did not finish by the plan's deadline, so the replication is reported on the training scenes only, where the detector is in-sample, with a @@F:F.horizon|str@@ s commitment.
- **F = no_room_design**: The open-loop test is replicated on nuScenes [110]. CenterPoint detections (of unconfirmed provenance) are tracked by CANMOT with its released nuScenes configuration and by the IMM tracker, and the planner is applied through an adapter: the route is the ego's logged path, and truth boxes are interpolated between annotated keyframes. Class averages and the commitment horizon were set on the training scenes, on which the detector was trained. The training scenes showed no measurable room at a 3 or 2 s commitment, so by the plan the replication stopped.
- **F = omitted**: A replication on nuScenes logs [110] was planned; it did not finish by the plan's deadline and is omitted (Supplement S10).

- **E3b.const.CK3 = safer_cost**: Behind leads that do not brake hard (@@E:E3b.n_cases|int@@ cases, lower level), the braking prediction is safer at a cost in time lost behind leads that keep their speed and is safer at no extra cost behind leads that brake mildly or stop and pull away; the per-phase schedule is safer at no extra cost behind all three kinds of lead (Table IV; descriptive).

## VI_WHY

- **base**: Measured at decision level, the tracker's covariance is equivalent to a class-average margin within 5% of the room on fresh runs (@@C:LB.RR_N.dec|dec1@@ @@C:LB.RR_N.dec.ci|ci1@@ decisions), at cut-in events and on real logs; it was not shown equivalent in closed loop, where it is safer at no extra cost. The claim concerns this covariance, not uncertainty in planning in general [17].
- **E = stopped_brake**: Measured at decision level, the tracker's covariance is equivalent to a class-average margin within 5% of the room on fresh runs (@@C:LB.RR_N.dec|dec1@@ @@C:LB.RR_N.dec.ci|ci1@@ decisions), at cut-in events and on real logs. The claim concerns this covariance, not uncertainty in planning in general [17].

The claim concerns this covariance, not uncertainty in planning in general [17].

## VI_ADAPTIVE

- **base**: A covariance that switches with the manoeuvre carries information the steady state lacks: the IMM recovers part of what it could at its amplitude. The braking prediction recovers more because it moves the predicted path rather than widening a variance around a constant-velocity path. Exploratory analyses of the old runs place the room where the tracker's velocity lags the lead's stop (Supplement S5).
- **H3 = uninformative**: The IMM's covariance varies enough to matter, yet it ranks decisions no better than a class average: its spread reacts to the manoeuvre but not to the realised error. A margin would need to vary in step with the error, which a prediction of the manoeuvre, like the braking prediction, does directly. Exploratory analyses of the old runs place the room where the tracker's velocity lags the lead's stop (Supplement S5).
- **H3 = amplitude_limited**: Even a covariance that switches with the manoeuvre varies too little for any ranking of decisions to recover much room at its amplitude; the room lies in the predicted path, which the braking prediction moves, not in the width of the margin. Exploratory analyses of the old runs place the room where the tracker's velocity lags the lead's stop (Supplement S5).
- **H3 = inconclusive**: Whether a covariance that switches with the manoeuvre can carry the room is not settled by these data: its share and its ceiling are both uncertain. Exploratory analyses of the old runs place the room where the tracker's velocity lags the lead's stop (Supplement S5).

## VI_COMMIT

- **base**: In closed loop, with the planner's own late reaction, the braking prediction reduces contacts at no extra cost, which supports the 3 s reading: information about the lead's motion is worth room when the car cannot revise in time.
- **E = stopped_brake**: A closed-loop test that would settle which reading applies was attempted but stopped (Section III-B), so the reading stays conditional: if decisions are in effect committed for seconds, information about the lead's motion is worth most of the room; if a prompt and reliable stop is available, little room remains, at the price of plans that rely on that stop.
- **EH1 = safer_cost**: In closed loop, with the planner's own late reaction, the braking prediction reduces contacts at a cost in time lost, which supports the 3 s reading: information about the lead's motion is worth room when the car cannot revise in time.
- **EH1 = equivalent**: In closed loop the braking prediction is equivalent to the class average, which supports the reaction-and-stop reading: when the car replans and brakes, little room is left for any source.
- **EH1 = worse**: In closed loop the braking prediction has more contacts, so neither open-loop reading is supported as it stands.
- **EH1 = inconclusive**: In closed loop the braking prediction is inconclusive, so neither open-loop reading is supported as it stands.

## VI_LIMITS

- **base**: Magnitudes are conditional on the 2 Hz update, the filter's tuning, leads that brake to a stop and the recording policy; only the statements listed in Section V-D hold in every run set, and the old and tuning runs are exploratory.
- **E = stopped_brake**: Magnitudes are conditional on the 2 Hz update, the filter's tuning, leads that brake to a stop, the stop assumed and the recording policy; only the statements listed in Section V-D hold in every run set, and the old and tuning runs are exploratory. The simplified-simulator check of Supplement S9 understates the tracker's error.
- **B.tuning = persists**: Magnitudes are conditional on the 2 Hz update, leads that brake to a stop and the recording policy; only the statements listed in Section V-D hold in every run set, and the old and tuning runs are exploratory.
- **B7.rate = holds**: Magnitudes are conditional on the filter's tuning, leads that brake to a stop and the recording policy; only the statements listed in Section V-D hold in every run set, and the old and tuning runs are exploratory.
